service_term: Georgia/Louisiana/Mississippi letters refer to public-defense law rather than restating length: twelve-month volunteers unless sooner discharged. Alabama refers to previous State raising regulations, not reprinted in its letter.
organisation: Infantry regiments; Georgia/Louisiana/Mississippi conform as far as possible to public-defense law; Alabama to prior raising regulations.
appointments: Referenced March6 law retains State-law unit appointments and Confederate general/staff authority. Alabama letter does not restate its prior appointment regulations.
arms_equipment: Transportation/subsistence federally provided from departure (explicit Alabama; accordingly in telegrams). Arms not separately allocated in these letters; incorporated law allows State OR Confederate supply, volunteers own clothing with commutation.
destination: Lynchburg; governor selects muster point
other_conditions: Without delay/earliest possible; answer requested. Louisiana one regiment, second only if ready. Activation draws on readiness; not all readiness totals added anew.
limits: Do not import Brown April23 election/Augusta proposal or Moore camp finance complaint into the April22 issuer text.

service_term: Not less than twelve months unless sooner discharged.
organisation: Ten infantry companies of at least64 men each; colonel/lieutenant-colonel/major, adjutant from lieutenants and sergeant-major from enlisted; each company captain/first lieutenant/two seconds/four sergeants/four corporals/two musicians.
appointments: Officers except staff appointed according to State law; staff by Confederate President.
arms_equipment: Volunteers furnish uniform with commutation; Confederate arms/ammunition sent to Harpers Ferry or governor-designated point; transport and subsistence from departure.
destination: Lynchburg;1regiment
other_conditions: Aid Virginia against stated common Southern enemy; answer whether and when; KY1/AR1/NC1/TN3 regiments.
limits: State permission to raise/send and Confederate military authority are distinct. The letter itself does not prove Tennessee legal authority existed.

other_conditions: Precaution for public safety; national30000;3000 each except TX2000/FL1000. Federal camp control and instruction.
limits: Do not convert hopes that many are armed into a mandatory State arms demand, or Moore/Brown later support conditions into original text.
